scope: Proposition 7.1 (Completion of the separated boundary) of the manuscript “Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree” (preprints/Deterministic-nonbipartite-Ramanujan-graphs-in-every-fixed-degree-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 178 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6d8ea4bb85aae750), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under these inputs, the account rule can deterministically complete the pairing. Every added edge is simple and preserves the girth exclusion. At the end the precision is positive at every primary point for both signs. There is a reference matrix b Pfin, defined below by exact numerical updates from a smooth coefficient truncation at the stop, such that at every retained primary parameter and both signs, max i,j |(Wfin − b Pfin)ij| ≤ CBB, BB = n.40a √ l2 . The construction retains the stop configuration and the matching added after it. These define the same family b Pfin(h) throughout the primary interval. All the accounts, candidate values and transitions in this section can be evaluated in a number of bit operations polynomial in n, with an exponent depending only on the fixed parameters.
